sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗，《纽约时报》出品。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: When the Supreme Court wrapped up its term last week, much of the focus was on the ruling that gave Donald Trump sweeping immunity from criminal prosecution.
sentences.zh: 上周最高法院结束本期开庭时，焦点大多集中在那项赋予唐纳德·特朗普刑事起诉广泛豁免权的裁决上。

sentences.en: But as my colleague Adam Liptak explains, a set of rulings that generated far less attention could have just as big an impact on American government and society.
sentences.zh: 但正如我的同事亚当·利普塔克所解释的那样，另一组受关注度少得多的裁决，可能会对美国政府和社会产生同样巨大的影响。

sentences.en: Monday, July 8th.
sentences.zh: 7月8日，星期一。

sentences.en: Adam, welcome back.
sentences.zh: 亚当，欢迎回来。

sentences.en: I mean, it hasn't been very long, but we want to talk to you about the rest of the
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，虽然过去没多久，但我们想和你聊聊关于

sentences.en: Supreme Court's decisions that happened over the past few weeks.
sentences.zh: 最高法院在过去几周里做出的其他决定。

sentences.en: The rest meaning the non-Trump decisions.
sentences.zh: “其他”是指与特朗普无关的决定。

sentences.en: There were a lot of other cases, many of which we covered on the show over the past year, but
sentences.zh: 还有许多其他案件，其中许多我们在过去一年里都在节目中报道过，但

sentences.en: we haven't yet talked about where the justices landed as they issued their rulings on these cases over the past few weeks.
sentences.zh: 我们还没讨论过大法官们在过去几周就这些案件做出裁决时的最终立场。

sentences.en: So I wonder if you can walk us through some of the bigger decisions and what, taken as a whole, this entire term really means.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，你能否带我们梳理一下其中一些重大的决定，以及从整体来看，整个这一期开庭究竟意味着什么。

sentences.en: So where should we start?
sentences.zh: 那我们应该从哪里开始呢？

sentences.en: Well, this term had so many major cases, Michael, on so many important issues touching all aspects of American politics and society that it's a little hard to know where to start.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，这一期开庭有太多重大案件，涉及那么多重要议题，触及美国政治和社会的方方面面，以至于有点让人不知从何说起。

sentences.en: But I think one way to think about the term is to ask, how much is this a 6-3 court?
sentences.zh: 但我认为，思考这一期开庭的一种方式是问：这在多大程度上是一个“6比3”的法院？

sentences.en: You know, the six conservatives in the majority, the three liberal justices in dissent, are we going to get that kind of classic lineup time after time after time?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，多数派的六位保守派大法官，加上持异议的三位自由派大法官，我们是不是会一次又一次、没完没了地看到这种经典的阵营对立？

sentences.en: And one way to start answering that question is to look at two areas which are kind of part
sentences.zh: 而回答这个问题的切入点之一，就是看两个领域，它们有点像

sentences.en: of the court's greatest hits, areas where they've done a lot of work in the last few terms, guns and abortion.
sentences.zh: 法院的“精选代表作”，也是他们在过去几期开庭中做了大量工作的领域：枪支和堕胎。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Let's start with guns.
sentences.zh: 让我们从枪支开始。

sentences.en: The court had two big guns cases.
sentences.zh: 法院审理了两起重大的枪支案件。

sentences.en: One of them involved the Second Amendment and broke eight to one against Second Amendment rights.
sentences.zh: 其中一起涉及宪法第二修正案，最终以8比1的投票结果反对第二修正案权利。

sentences.en: Only Justice Clarence Thomas, the most avid supporter of gun rights, was in dissent.
sentences.zh: 只有枪支权利最坚定的支持者、大法官克拉伦斯·托马斯投了反对票。

sentences.en: So let me tell you just a little bit about this case.
sentences.zh: 所以我来简单讲讲这个案子。

sentences.en: Please.
sentences.zh: 请讲。

sentences.en: There's a federal law that says people subject to domestic violence restraining orders, it's a crime for them to have guns.
sentences.zh: 有一项联邦法律规定，受家庭暴力限制令约束的人拥有枪支是违法的。

sentences.en: A guy named Zaki Rahimi was subject to such a domestic violence restraining order, but he goes to court and says, this law violates my Second Amendment rights.
sentences.zh: 一个叫扎基·拉希米的人收到了这样的家庭暴力限制令，但他却去法院说，这项法律侵犯了他的第二修正案权利。

sentences.en: The Second Amendment protects me and allows me to have a gun, even if I'm in this status.
sentences.zh: 第二修正案保护我，允许我拥有枪支，即使我有这种身份也不例外。

sentences.en: And that goes to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 于是案子闹到了最高法院。

sentences.en: And the way the Supreme Court analyzes this question is it looks to a test that it established only
sentences.zh: 最高法院分析这个问题的方法是，参考它在仅仅

sentences.en: a couple of years ago in 2022, which said, you judge the constitutionality of gun control laws using history.
sentences.zh: 两年前的2022年才确立的一项测试，该测试规定：你要用历史来判断枪支管控法律的合宪性。

sentences.en: You kind of go back in time and you see whether the community in the founding era disarmed people in the same way that the current law disarms people.
sentences.zh: 你得回溯历史，看看建国时期的大众剥夺人们武装的方式，是否与现行法律剥夺人们武装的方式相同。

sentences.en: And you might think that actually, back in the 1700s, there were no such things as domestic violence restraining orders.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为，在18世纪的时候，根本没有什么家庭暴力限制令这种东西。

sentences.en: So you might think that the answer is this contemporary law is unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会觉得，答案是当代这项法律违宪。

sentences.en: But Chief Justice John Roberts, writing for an eight justice majority, says, no, that's not quite right.
sentences.zh: 但由八位大法官多数派执笔的主审法官、首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨说：“不，这不太对。”

sentences.en: We're going to kind of roll back the specificity of the test and look at very general principles.
sentences.zh: 我们要稍微退回一步，淡化测试的特异性，转而审视非常普遍的原则。

sentences.en: Can you disarm dangerous people back then?
sentences.zh: 当年能解除危险分子的武装吗？

sentences.en: And if you can do that, then you can disarm Rahimi, even under this law that the founding generation could not have contemplated.
sentences.zh: 如果你能做到这一点，那么你就可以解除拉希米的武装，即使根据这项建国一代根本无法预料的法律也是如此。

sentences.en: That's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真有意思。

sentences.en: So the court, as conservative majority especially, seems to be saying that our last big decision made it too hard to regulate guns.
sentences.zh: 因此，法院，尤其是保守派多数派，似乎在说：我们上一个重大决定让枪支监管变得太难了。

sentences.en: We need to fix that.
sentences.zh: 我们需要修复这一点。

sentences.en: So we're going to search really hard for a way to make sure that somebody with a restraining order for domestic abuse can't legally have a gun.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要竭尽全力寻找一种方法，确保因虐待家庭而被下达限制令的人无法合法拥有枪支。

sentences.en: On the other hand, there was a second guns case, not involving the Second Amendment, but posing an important issue.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，还有第二起枪支案件，它不涉及第二修正案，但提出了一个重要问题。

sentences.en: The question in the case was whether the Trump administration was allowed to enact a gun control
sentences.zh: 该案的核心问题是：在2017年拉斯维加斯枪击案发生之后，特朗普政府是否被允许颁布一项枪支管控

sentences.en: regulation in 2017 after the Las Vegas shooting in which, at an outdoor music festival, a gunman killed 58 people, wounded 500 more.
sentences.zh: 法规？在那次户外音乐节上，一名枪手杀害了58人，并打伤了500多人。

sentences.en: And the Trump administration, prompted by this massacre, they issue a regulation that tries to outlaw bump stocks.
sentences.zh: 在这次大屠杀的促使下，特朗普政府颁布了一项试图取缔撞火枪托的法规。

sentences.en: What are bump stocks?
sentences.zh: 什么是撞火枪托？

sentences.en: They're devices that turn semi-automatic weapons into weapons that can fire at rates approaching a machine gun.
sentences.zh: 它们是能将半自动武器变成发射速度接近机关枪的武器的装置。

sentences.en: And drawing on the authority of a 1934 law, which bans, for the most part, civilian ownership
sentences.zh: 借助1934年一项法律的授权，该法基本上禁止平民拥有

sentences.en: of machine guns, it said bump stocks are basically the same thing, and we will, by regulation, outlaw them.
sentences.zh: 机关枪，它说撞火枪托基本上是一回事，我们将通过法规将其取缔。

sentences.en: And the question for the court was, did the 1934 law authorize that?
sentences.zh: 法院面临的问题是：1934年的法律授权这样做吗？

sentences.en: And here, and this is a typical split on this kind of stuff, the majority, the conservative majority, takes a textualist approach.
sentences.zh: 在这里，这也是这类问题典型的分裂，多数派、保守派多数派采取了原旨主义的方法。

sentences.en: It bears down on the particular words of the statute, and Justice Thomas looks at the words
sentences.zh: 它紧抓成文法的具体字眼不放，大法官托马斯审视了

sentences.en: that Congress said, a machine gun is one where a single function of the trigger causes all of these bullets to fly, and a bump stock, he said, is not precisely that.
sentences.zh: 国会所说的话：机关枪是指扣动一次扳机就能让所有这些子弹飞出去的枪，而他认为，撞火枪托并不完全是这种情况。

sentences.en: Therefore, we're going to strike down this regulation.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们要推翻这项法规。

sentences.en: So how do you reconcile these two divergent gun rulings, one where the court works really hard to allow for gun restrictions in the case of domestic abusers, and another where they
sentences.zh: 那么，你如何调和这两起截然不同的枪支裁决？一起是法院费尽心思允许在涉嫌家庭暴力者身上实施枪支限制，而另一起则是

sentences.en: seem to have no compunction about allowing for a bump stock that I think most of us, practically speaking, understand as making a semi-automatic weapon automatic in the real world?
sentences.zh: 他们似乎毫无内疚地允许使用撞火枪托——在我看来，我们大多数人在现实中都明白，这实际上是将半自动武器变成了全自动武器？

sentences.en: I think the court draws a real distinction between two kinds of cases.
sentences.zh: 我认为法院在两类案件之间划清了真正的界限。

sentences.en: One is about interpreting the Constitution, interpreting the Second Amendment.
sentences.zh: 一是关于解释宪法，解释第二修正案。

sentences.en: And in that area, it is plowing new ground.
sentences.zh: 在那个领域，它正在开辟新天地。

sentences.en: It has issued maybe four major Second Amendment cases, and it's trying to figure out how that works and what the limits are.
sentences.zh: 它可能已经发布了四起重大的第二修正案案件，并且正在摸索它的运作方式以及界限在哪里。

sentences.en: And the Rahimi case shows you that they're still finding their way.
sentences.zh: 拉希米案向你表明，他们仍在摸索前行。

sentences.en: They're trying to find the right balance in that constitutional realm where they are the last word.
sentences.zh: 他们正试图在那个拥有最终解释权的宪法领域找到适当的平衡。

sentences.en: The bump stocks case doesn't involve the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 撞火枪托案不涉及宪法。

sentences.en: It involves an interpretation of a statute enacted by Congress, and the majority in those kinds of cases tends to read statutes narrowly.
sentences.zh: 它涉及对国会颁布的成文法的解释，而这类案件中的多数派往往倾向于狭义地解读法律。

sentences.en: And they would say that that's acceptable because unlike in a constitutional case, if it's about a congressional statute, Congress can go back and fix it.
sentences.zh: 他们会说这是可以接受的，因为与宪法案件不同，如果涉及国会法律，国会可以回过头来修复它。

sentences.en: Congress can say whatever it likes.
sentences.zh: 国会可以随心所欲地说任何它想说的话。

sentences.en: Justice Samuel Alito said in the bump stocks case, this massacre was terrible.
sentences.zh: 大法官萨缪尔·阿利托在撞火枪托案中表示，这场大屠杀太可怕了。

sentences.en: And it's a pity Congress didn't act.
sentences.zh: 国会没有采取行动真是一种遗憾。

sentences.en: But if Congress doesn't act, a regulator can't step in and do what Congress didn't do.
sentences.zh: 但如果国会不采取行动，监管机构就不能介入去做国会没有做的事。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That's interesting because it suggests a surprising level of open-mindedness among even the court's
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为它表明即使在法院

sentences.en: most conservative justices to an interpretation of the Constitution that may allow for a greater level of gun regulation than perhaps we think of them as being interested in.
sentences.zh: 最保守的大法官中，也表现出令人惊奇的开明程度，他们对宪法的解释可能允许比我们想象中他们所感兴趣的更高水平的枪支监管。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When we're talking about the Constitution, they do seem more open to regulating guns than you might have thought.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论宪法时，他们确实表现得比你想象的更乐于监管枪支。

sentences.en: Okay, you also mentioned, Adam, abortion.
sentences.zh: 好吧，亚当，你还提到了堕胎。

sentences.en: Let's talk about those decisions from this court.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈法院做出的这些决定。

sentences.en: So the court in 2022, as everyone knows, overturned Roe v.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，法院在2022年推翻了罗诉

sentences.en: Wade, eliminated the constitutional right to abortion.
sentences.zh: 韦德案，取消了宪法规定的堕胎权。

sentences.en: But in two cases this term, they effectively enhanced the availability of abortion.
sentences.zh: 但在本期开庭的两起案件中，他们实际上扩大了堕胎的可及性。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: One of them involves emergency rooMs.
sentences.zh: 其中一起涉及急诊室。

sentences.en: There's a federal statute that says that emergency rooms that receive federal money have to treat patients and give them stabilizing care if they arrive in the emergency room.
sentences.zh: 有一项联邦法律规定，接受联邦资金的急诊室必须在病人到达急诊室时对其进行治疗并提供稳定病情的护理。

sentences.en: That seems to conflict with a strict Idaho law that prohibits abortions except to save the life of the mother.
sentences.zh: 这似乎与爱达荷州一项严格的法律相冲突，该法律禁止堕胎，除非是为了挽救母亲的生命。

sentences.en: The court agrees to hear the case.
sentences.zh: 法院同意审理此案。

sentences.en: The court agrees to hear the case.
sentences.zh: 法院同意审理此案。

sentences.en: It hears arguments.
sentences.zh: 它听取了辩论。

sentences.en: And then it dismisses the case.
sentences.zh: 然后它驳回了此案。

sentences.en: It dismisses it as improvidently granted, which is judicial speak for never mind.
sentences.zh: 它以“草率批准”为由将其驳回，这是司法上的说法，意思是“算了”。

sentences.en: But it's very tentative.
sentences.zh: 但这非常具有试探性。

sentences.en: The court merely dismissed the case.
sentences.zh: 法院仅仅驳回了此案。

sentences.en: It said it was too early to hear it.
sentences.zh: 它说现在审理还为时过早。

sentences.en: They're going to look at it later.
sentences.zh: 他们以后会再看。

sentences.en: So it's a very tentative sliver of a victory for abortion rights.
sentences.zh: 所以这对堕胎权来说是一个非常具试探性的微小胜利。

sentences.en: But nonetheless, the effect of this is to suspend the Idaho law, at least to the extent it conflicts with the federal law, and it lets emergency abortions continue.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，此举的效果是暂停了爱达荷州的法律，至少在它与联邦法律相冲突的范围内，并让紧急堕胎得以继续。

sentences.en: Women in Idaho have more access to emergency abortions as a consequence of this decision than if the court had gone the other way.
sentences.zh: 由于这项裁决，爱达荷州的女性比法院走向另一个方向时拥有更多的途径来进行紧急堕胎。

sentences.en: And of course, the other abortion case centered on the abortion pill, mifepristone.
sentences.zh: 当然，另一起堕胎案的核心是堕胎药米非司酮。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that pill is used in a majority of abortions, and the availability of that pill is crucial to what remains of abortion rights in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这种药丸用于大多数堕胎手术，而这种药丸的可及性对于美国剩余的堕胎权至关重要。

sentences.en: Lower courts had said that the Food and Drug Administration exceeded its authority in approving these abortion pills.
sentences.zh: 下级法院曾表示，食品药品监督管理局在批准这些堕胎药时超出了其职权范围。

sentences.en: And the case comes to the Supreme Court, and here again, they rule in favor of abortion rights.
sentences.zh: 案件闹到了最高法院，在这里他们再次裁决支持堕胎权。

sentences.en: They maintain the availability of these pills.
sentences.zh: 他们维持了这些药物的可及性。

sentences.en: But they do so again in a kind of technical way that does not assure that the pills will forever remain available.
sentences.zh: 但他们再次以一种技术性的方式做到这一点，并不能保证这些药物永远都可以获得。

sentences.en: What the court says merely, and unanimously, is that the particular plaintiffs who challenged
sentences.zh: 法院只是全票表示，那些对

sentences.en: the law, doctors and medical groups who oppose abortion, didn't have standing, hadn't suffered
sentences.zh: 法律提出挑战的特定原告——反对堕胎的医生和医疗团体——不具备诉讼主体资格，没有遭受

sentences.en: the sort of direct injury that gave them the right to sue, and it got rid of the case on standing grounds.
sentences.zh: 那种赋予他们起诉权利的直接伤害，并以不具备诉讼主体资格为由驳回了此案。

sentences.en: But that's not a permanent decision.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是一个永久性的决定。

sentences.en: Other people, other groups can sue, have sued, and the court didn't decide whether the FDA approval was proper or not, only that the lawsuit couldn't go forward.
sentences.zh: 其他人、其他团体可以起诉，也已经起诉了，而且法院并未裁定FDA的批准是否合适，只是裁定诉讼无法继续进行。

sentences.en: And here, too, this case is a victory for abortion rights, but maybe an ephemeral one and may well
sentences.zh: 在这里也是一样，这个案子是堕胎权的胜利，但也许是短暂的胜利，很可能会

sentences.en: return to the court, which is not given an indication of how it will turn out if they actually address the merits.
sentences.zh: 再次回到法院，而法院并未表明如果他们真正处理案情实质将会如何裁决。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So this is a court, the one you're describing in these rulings, acting with some nuance and some restraint.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个法院，正如你所描述的在这些裁决中，表现出了一些细微差别和某种克制。

sentences.en: Yeah, this picture is complicated.
